  Two things the investigation changed about the design

  Trust. Portal's auto-attachment query sets no Types filter, so
  agent-manager.runs, signal-inbox.signals and web-search.live already reach a
  system prompt today with one sentence of prose as the only mitigation.
  Consumers that execute shell commands can't inherit that. Trust is derived
  from provider_id through a static table, external content is excluded from
  agent consumers outright, and Phase 11 attacks the rendered brief through
  prompt-injection-arena rather than asserting it's safe.

  Proof over assumption. Prompt-time injection is proven only for claude-code.
  All five runtimes use PreToolUse only and none declares its hook-event
  capability anywhere. Phase 1 runs a live canary before anything is built on
  it, and the installer refuses an unverified runtime rather than writing a
  hook that never fires — which is exactly the failure you spent weeks living
  with.

  Hook repairs, and one thing you should know

  Your PreToolUse error is fixed at source and live. Two more defects found,
  both filed as Phase 1 work rather than patched:

  - agentharness/hook_broker.go:632 maps four unrelated command strings onto
    the single id vrooli-policy-runner. That's why removing the stale entry
    also took your deny-guard. It's restored, deny list untouched at 23.
  - web-console/api/hook_prompt_submit_handler.go:34 returns 400 without a
    webConsoleSessionId. Measured both branches. A Claude Code session started
    from a plain terminal in this repo fails its UserPromptSubmit hook on every
    prompt — you only don't see it because you're in a web-console terminal.

  To start: plan-manager exec continue
  agent-context-briefs-one-portal-owned-brief-served-to-llm, paired with
  prompt-manager skill read implementation-plan-execution so the executing
  agent has the divergence rules before it hits the first wrong assumption.
